To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expansion of cord blood CD 34 + HPC in coculture with HUVEC is superior to cytokines supplemented liquid culture.

the expansion of cord blood hematopoietic stem cells (HSC) and progenitor cells in vitro in an autochtonous coculture system with umbilical vein (cord) endothelial cells (HVEC, HUVEC) is superior (superiority) to cytokine-supplementated liquid culture.
expansion of hematopoietetic progenitor cells (CD34+) from cord blood in coculture with endothelium results in a significant increase in total cells, CD34+, and clonogenic precursors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of an autologous ex vivo expansion system for cord blood progenitor cells.
the development of an ex vivo culture system to expand human cord blood (CB) hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (CB HPC).
the expansion of human cord blood hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells in the presence of umbilical cord vein endothelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study shows a significant expansion of hematopoietetic progenitors in the presence of autologous endothelium, but the results are not yet conclusive enough for clinical application.
cord blood progenitor expansion in coculture is a feasable approach and that the combination of SCF, Flt-3L and IL-6 in liquid culture is a good alternative to SCF alone.
the use of autologous endothelial cells for ex vivo expansion results in superior expansion of CD34+ HSC and progenitor cells compared to liquid culture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of HUVEC and VEGF and/or IL-1 in coculture with HPC is superior to the use of cytokines alone in liquid culture for expansion of CD34+ cells and clonogenic precursors.
the expansion of CD34+ hematopietic progenitor (HPC) cells in the presence of autologous umblical vein endothelial cells is superior to cytokin-supplemented liquid culture.
cord blood progenitors are expanded in coculture with endothelium and the expanded cells have the potential to restore hematopoiesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of autologous endothelial cells in the expansion of cord blood progenitors may provide a safer alternative to the use of xenogenic endothelial cells or cell lines.
the use of autologous endothelium for cord blood expansion is feasible, and that the expansion is superior to liquid culture.

expansion of cord blood CD 34+ hematopoetic progenitor cells in a coculture with autolougous umbilical endothelial cells results in higher numbers of progenitor cells than cytokine supplemented liquid culture.
